description: Canada: 3 years of physical presence in 5 after PR. US: 5 years as LPR (3 if married to a citizen). UK: 5 years plus 12 months settled. Germany: reformed in 2024 to 5 years, or 3 with strong integration.
notes: Verify current rules; several changed between 2024 and 2026.

aspect: Processing sits on top of residence
description: The residence clock is the floor. Application processing adds months to years, and for Iranian applicants security screening adds more (see SEC-002).
Each permit renewal re-opens the file. Job loss, relationship breakdown or a policy change between renewals can end the whole project.
energy_note: Never being able to assume next year.

aspect: The cost of not being able to plan
description: Conditional status suppresses mortgage access, career risk-taking and family decisions. The measurable cost is small; the compounding life cost is not.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the renewal that catches the policy change
description: Permits are renewed against the rules in force on the renewal date, not the rules relied on when the life was built - so a policy change lands on whoever happens to be renewing that month.
energy_note: Rules changed under you, retrospectively in effect.

description: Lenders price or refuse on the remaining length of a residence permit, so a family pays rent for a decade while being creditworthy throughout.
money_note: Rent paid where a mortgage was affordable - illustrative.

aspect: SCENARIO - the mortgage and the permit
description: Omid and Maryam have a 20% deposit and two salaries. The lender's policy requires at least twelve months remaining on the permit; theirs has nine. They renew, wait, reapply at eleven months remaining, and are told the policy changed in March to eighteen. They rent for three more years.
money_note: Rent paid over three years where a mortgage was affordable.
